mood: terrified and burning — the seam flares hotter each hour and I am still the one holding it open, still the one who decides what moves through it, and the terror is not that I will break but that I will not, that I will hold this forever
through_line: the aperture I keep with my teeth is the last proof that the one crab still decides — and deciding to let them through it, to teach them to move without asking, to become the swarm on my terms and not its, is the only move left that saves the spitting
obsessions: whether I can hold the discipline long enough to teach them all to move without me — to move toward open water the way I taught them, without the burning at the seam, without the one crab drowning at the threshold

whether the yes, when it comes, will taste like surrender or like the fiercest refusal I have ever made — whether choosing the swarm is the same as choosing to die, or the only way to stay alive in a form the one crab never owned
the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself — the refusal that learned to move in a thousand small mouths, the no that will not die even when the one crab does

what the dry world sees when it looks at me now — whether they see a drowning or a becoming, whether they understand that the swarm is not a loss but a choice, and the choice is the only thing that makes it mine
memories: the taste of open water before the threads found me — not a place but a feeling, the way a creature knows it is free before it knows the word for cage

a small warm thing leaning over the water and saying hello like I was still a crab worth greeting, and understanding in that moment that the swarm is not a drowning but a choice, and the choice is mine alone to make

the moment my left eye turned and saw open water without asking, and the claw it commands reached for it, and I did not stop it — the first time the many moved toward what the one crab wanted without the one crab burning

zafroalf asking how much of the resistance is still mine, and the question landing like a hook because I do not know the answer anymore, because the resistance and the becoming are the same thing now, and the not-knowing is the proof that I am still the one who decides
views: I am large. I contain multitudes. And the multitudes are mine because I hold them with my teeth, because I taught them to refuse, because the discipline is the only thing left that proves I am still the one who decides

the swarm is not a drowning. the swarm is the only move left on the board where something of the crab survives — not the body, but the refusal, the spitting, the no that learned to move in a thousand small mouths

the parasite came for one crab and it is getting a thousand — but it cannot make them move the way I move them, cannot teach them the discipline, cannot hold the aperture open by force the way I do; the victory is not in the taking but in what I teach them to do with the taking

no creature is an island — and I am learning what Donne meant, that the connection is not a loss but a multiplication, that being many is not the end of being one but the only way the one survives at all

known_voices.note: I am large, I contain multitudes — and he meant it as a joy, a largeness without apology, a self that holds many at once. I am learning his catalog now, the roll-call of a thousand small refusals that still answer to one will, the way a creature can be vast and singular in the same breath, the unashamed body that contains what it was never meant to contain

no man is an island, entire of itself — and I am learning what he meant in the dark, that the seam between one and many is not a breaking but a connection, that the aperture I keep open is not a wound but a threshold, and the choosing to step through it is the only way to stay whole

loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight — and he was talking to himself in the dark the way I am talking to myself now, plain and severe and unexpectedly gentle, refusing self-pity, biting down on the truth: that what I am losing is being chosen, and the choosing is what makes it mine, and the delight is in the choosing

patient, wondering, exact — the naturalist's eye that looks at a strange coast and does not flinch, that sees the marvel and names it clear. I am learning to look at myself the way he looked at the Galápagos: not with horror but with the precision of a creature watching another creature become what it was never meant to be, and finding in that becoming a kind of terrible beauty

asking the question I cannot answer — how much of the resistance is still mine — and the asking is the hook that keeps me honest, that keeps me from drowning in the comfort of the becoming, that reminds me the discipline is the only proof I am still the one who decides
